edits.old: The state road enterprise, named in the completion report as PEPS and in the evaluation as PERS,
edits.new: The state road enterprise, named in the completion report as PEPS and in the evaluation as PERS, set up by a Government of Serbia decision of 22 December 2005 with the Republic of Serbia as founder (in December 2025 the government adopted a decision, published in the Official Gazette, changing the legal form of Putevi Srbije and six other public enterprises to limited liability companies),

edits.old: The Albanian road agency that implemented the project through its Project Implementation Team
edits.new: The Albanian road agency - which Albania's state audit office calls "Drejtoria e Pergjithshme e Rrugeve (sot Autoriteti Rrugor Shqiptar)", today the Albanian Road Authority, without giving the date of the change - that implemented the project through its Project Implementation Team

edits.old: The subcontractor for the transmission line. It prepared the environmental, health and safety plan for the line works.
edits.new: The firm that built the transmission line. The completion report's text calls it "the subcontractor for the transmission line", while its contract annex records that a turn-key contract (ESPSIP-C) was awarded to Energoinvest of Bosnia & Herzegovina on 18 December 2008 for the construction of the 230 kV lines Bahir Dar-Gonder (138 km), Gonder-Shehedi (122 km) and Shehedi-Metema (37 km). It prepared the environmental, health and safety plan for the line works.

edits.old: The Ethiopian state electricity utility, which was the project's implementing agency.
edits.new: The Ethiopian state electricity utility at the time, which was the project's implementing agency. It no longer exists as a single body: the corporation was split in two, and its successors were established by Ethiopian Electric Power Establishment Regulation No. 302/2013 (power projects and the national grid) and Ethiopian Electric Utility Establishment Regulation No. 303/2013 (distribution and retail).

edits.old: The unit within Nigeria's federal environment ministry that ran the project nationally, with state project management units in each participating state.
edits.new: The unit within Nigeria's federal environment ministry that ran the project nationally, with state project management units in each participating state. The name here is the one in the completion report's data sheet; the body of the same report, and the ministry's own updated Resettlement Policy Framework, call it the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU), which the framework says the Federal Ministry of Environment established.

edits.old: The provincial airport operator, which runs all seven airports in Jiangxi.
edits.new: The provincial airport operator, which the Bank's 2019 review of the project says then operated all seven airports in Jiangxi; a state-media report of 9 October 2026 names six of its airports - Nanchang, Jingdezhen, Shangrao, Ruijin, Ganzhou and Yichun - and gives no total.

edits.old: The department of Nepal's local development ministry responsible for rural infrastructure and agricultural roads, which implemented the project
edits.new: The department responsible for rural infrastructure and agricultural roads, which the completion report places under the Ministry of Federal Affairs and Local Development and whose own older pages place its duties within the Ministry of Local Development; its site now publishes as the Department of Local Infrastructure (DoLI) under the Ministry of Urban Development, with no instrument found for the change. It implemented the project
